answer: Attackers creating many identities face the full cost per account, so a flood of puppets becomes a rising tide they must fund themselves. Sybil resistance comes from staking bonded reputation on a shared ridge ledger: each agent must lock tokens to register, and voting weight scales with stake aged across epochs. Honest peers then mirror that ledger locally, cross-checking stake proofs; any mismatch flags the cluster and slashes deposits. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
